cohort: The study included 7796 nulliparous women >=40 years and 264,262 nulliparous women 25-29 years in Sweden, all with a singleton, term, live fetus in cephalic presentation and a planned vaginal delivery.
finding: Nulliparous women >=40 years had significantly higher risks of intrapartum cesarean section and operative vaginal delivery compared to women 25-29 years, regardless of labor onset, while the risks of obstetric anal sphincter injury or a 5-minute Apgar score <7 were not increased.
mod_finding: The risks of intrapartum cesarean section and operative vaginal delivery were significantly higher in nulliparous women aged 40 years or older compared with women 25-29 years, after both spontaneous onset and induction of labor.
followup_time: Perinatal, with Apgar score observed at 5 minutes post-birth
